name: Esomeprazole + Domperidone
meta: Esomeprazole Magnesium: Proton pump inhibitor (PPI); Domperidone: Peripheral dopamine D2 antagonist (prokinetic / antiemetic)
Schedule H – prescription only; Domperidone: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White to slightly coloured crystalline powder (magnesium trihydrate).
White or almost white powder, practically insoluble in water.

Esomeprazole Magnesium: The S-enantiomer of omeprazole, giving higher and more consistent plasma levels. First approval/introduction: Patented 1993; approved 2000 (EU), US FDA February 2001 (AstraZeneca). Domperidone: In 2014 the EMA restricted use to relief of nausea and vomiting at a maximum of 10 mg three times daily, generally for ≤1 week, because of cardiac risks. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1974 (Janssen Pharmaceutica); marketed 1979 (Switzerland, West Germany); not approved in the USA.
Potent acid suppression combined with improved gastric emptying.

Esomeprazole Magnesium S-isomer of omeprazole; irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+-ATPase, providing more consistent acid suppression. Receptor / target profile: Irreversibly blocks H+/K+-ATPase in gastric parietal cells.

Domperidone Blocks peripheral D2 receptors in the upper GI tract (increasing oesophageal sphincter tone and gastric emptying) and in the chemoreceptor trigger zone (outside the blood–brain barrier). Receptor / target profile: Peripherally selective D2 and D3 antagonist; acts on the chemoreceptor trigger zone (outside the blood–brain barrier) and upper GI tract; raises prolactin.
Summary: Bioavailability ~64% (single dose) rising to ~89% (repeated). Tmax 1–2 h. ~97% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C19/3A4. Half-life 1–1.5 h.
Summary: Bioavailability ~15% (first-pass); Tmax ~1 h (SR prolonged). ~92% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP3A4. Half-life 7–9 h.
Functional dyspepsia not responding to PPI alone
One capsule once daily before breakfast
Short-term use; review cardiac risk factors
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Severe: reduce frequency to once or twice daily.
>60 years: higher arrhythmia risk – use lowest dose.
≥12 years and ≥35 kg: adult dosing; younger: 0.25 mg/kg up to three times daily (specialist).
Excreted in small amounts; use with caution.
Known QT prolongation, significant electrolyte disturbance, underlying cardiac disease (e.g. heart failure)
Concomitant QT-prolonging drugs or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
Serious ventricular arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death – risk higher >60 years and >30 mg/day; use lowest dose, max ~1 week
Raised prolactin – galactorrhoea, gynaecomastia, menstrual irregularity
Clopidogrel – reduced antiplatelet effect; avoid combination
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir) – contraindicated
Esomeprazole Magnesium: At least 1 hour before meals.
Domperidone: ECG if cardiac risk factors; potassium, magnesium.
Esomeprazole Magnesium: Supportive care. Domperidone: Drowsiness, disorientation, EPS (especially children), arrhythmias. ECG monitoring; supportive care.
Swallow whole – do not crush or chew
Do not use long-term without review
Use for the shortest time (usually ≤1 week)
Inform doctor of all heart medicines and antifungals/antibiotics
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
